sections.html:
Jackson County sits on the Gulf Coast in the southeastern corner of Mississippi, about 190 miles from the state capital. It has no connection to the city of Jackson, which is in Hinds County. The county seat is Pascagoula, and the other cities are Gautier, Moss Point and Ocean Springs. Vancleave, Escatawpa, Gulf Park Estates and Latimer are among the unincorporated communities.

The population was 143,252 in 2020 and is estimated at 147,666 for 2025, up from 118,015 in 1980. The county is heavily industrial, with shipbuilding, refinery and manufacturing jobs around Pascagoula, Moss Point and Ocean Springs. Steady employment like that brings buyers who want to live close to work. Storm-exposed and older houses tend to sit longer on the market.

Interstate 10 and US 90 run east and west through the county, and state highways 57, 63 and 609 run north. Much of the county is water or protected land, so a lot of the housing is packed along the coast and the main roads.

sections.h2: Tax assessor and tax collector offices
sections.html:
Jackson County is one of 17 Mississippi counties that keep the tax assessor and the tax collector as separate offices. You will deal with both when you sell: the assessor sets the value and the exemptions, and the collector sends the bill and takes the payment.

OfficeWhat it handlesContact
Tax AssessorReal property appraisal, business personal property, homestead exemptionDepartments for Real Property Appraisal, Personal Property (Business) and Homestead
Tax CollectorBills and collects real and personal property tax2915 Canty Street, Pascagoula; mail to Box 998, Pascagoula, MS 39568; 228-769-3074; Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Both offices have pages on the county website: Tax Collector and Tax Assessor. Parts of those pages load slowly, so call before you drive over. That goes double if you want to know whether the collector has a drop box for payments.

Mississippi assesses property to whoever owns it on January 1. Bills go out in November or December and are due by February 1. If February 1 lands on a weekend or holiday, you can pay the next Monday without interest. After that, interest runs at one-half of one percent per month under Mississippi Code 27-41-9.

  • January 1: assessment date and ownership date.
  • April 1: deadline for homestead exemption, builder affidavits and business personal property renditions.
  • First Monday in July: the assessment rolls are presented.
  • First Monday in August: the Board of Supervisors starts hearing appeals.
  • February 1: payment due date.

The calendar matters most when a sale closes near one of these dates. Put in the contract who pays the February 1 bill, and have the title company write it into the closing statement.

sections.h2: How hurricanes affect taxes and house sales
sections.html:
Storms are part of this county's property record. Hurricane Camille hit in August 1969 and Hurricane Katrina on August 29, 2005, and both did catastrophic damage along the coast.

State law builds in some relief for payment delays. Under Mississippi Code 27-41-9, the governor may extend the date for charging interest by proclamation when unusual conditions delay payment through no fault of the taxpayer or the collector. The extension can run up to 60 days, with two more extensions possible. The state tax agency has also published guidance on possible relief under section 27-35-143(9), which lets boards of supervisors adjust assessments in certain circumstances. Ask the chancery clerk whether that section applies to your parcel.

Unrepaired roof or water damage lowers a house's value and can block a buyer's financing, because a lender's inspector may refuse to sign off. That is why owners here sometimes sell as-is. If you think storm damage should lower your assessment, the appeal window closes on the first Monday in August.

sections.h2: Why neighbors can pay different amounts
sections.html:
Four public school districts divide the county. The Jackson County School District covers Hurley, Wade, Big Point, Three Rivers, Harleston, Vestry, Latimer and Vancleave, plus St. Martin and a small part of Escatawpa. Pascagoula-Gautier serves Pascagoula and most of Gautier, Moss Point serves Moss Point and most of Escatawpa, and Ocean Springs serves Ocean Springs.

The county, each city and each school district set their own levy, and they add together into one millage rate. Two houses of the same value in different districts can owe different amounts. Check which district your address falls in before you estimate a buyer's tax bill.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Jackson County taxes?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax puts the property in line for the county tax auction. State law allows sales on the first Monday in April and the last Monday in August. Call the county tax collector for the date that applies to your parcel.

After a sale, the owner has two years from the sale date to redeem by paying the delinquent taxes plus statutory damages and interest. The chancery clerk is supposed to notify the owner of that right. If nobody redeems, the buyer can receive a tax deed. For land sold to the state, the Secretary of State can be reached at 1-866-835-2637.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes, liens or storm damage
sections.html:
You can sell a house that has back taxes. The title search turns up the amount, and it is paid from the sale proceeds. Liens and an unpaid mortgage balance are handled the same way.

  1. Ask the tax collector for a payoff figure on any back taxes before you list or accept an offer.
  2. Confirm your homestead status. An owner-occupied single-family home is assessed at 10 percent of value instead of 15 percent, and the filing window runs January 1 to April 1.
  3. Collect insurance and repair records if the house had flood or wind damage.
  4. Hire an attorney or a title company to prepare the deed.
  5. At closing, taxes, liens and any mortgage payoff come out of your proceeds, and the title company records the new deed.

A cash buyer does not wait on a lender, which can shorten the closing when a house cannot pass a financing inspection. Cash Home Buyers looks at each Jackson County property individually and does not set a price or a timeline until we have the details.

faqs.q: Is Jackson County, MS the same as Jackson, MS?
faqs.a: No. Jackson County is on the Mississippi Gulf Coast with Pascagoula as its seat, about 190 miles from the city of Jackson, which is in Hinds County. Each place has its own property tax office.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Jackson County, Mississippi?
faqs.a: By February 1 each year. If that date falls on a weekend or holiday, you may pay the next Monday without interest, and later payments carry one-half of one percent interest per month.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Jackson County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Tax Collector at 2915 Canty Street in Pascagoula, or mail it to Box 998, Pascagoula, MS 39568. The phone is 228-769-3074, and the office is open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Jackson County assessment?
faqs.a: Request a hearing with the Board of Supervisors through the Chancery Clerk. The normal deadline is the first Monday in August, when the Board begins hearing appeals.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jackson County, MS house after hurricane damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Damaged houses sell as-is to buyers who accept the repairs, and any back taxes are paid from the proceeds. A title company confirms liens before closing.
